description:
FILED s451w, as the measured residue of #685 (which took op/leaky-magic.t 65/6 -> 70/1).

MECHANISM.  #685 fixed %p-symref-symbol, the runtime resolver behind the
SYMBOLIC spellings ${"foo::!"} / @{"foo::+"} / %{"foo::SIG"}.  The LITERAL
spelling `%foo::SIG` never reaches it: the emitter puts the name in the CL
source as `foo::%SIG`, and the CL READER's `intern` in package |FOO| RETURNS
THE INHERITED PCL SYMBOL (every Perl package is made `(:use :cl :pcl)`), so
the emitted `(defvar foo::%SIG (make-hash-table â¦))` declares PCL's own %SIG
(a no-op, it is already bound) and every later read of `foo::%SIG` is main's.

MEASURED (s451w, after #685):
    $SIG{__WARN__} = sub {};
    print scalar(keys %foo::SIG), "\n";
        perl: 0        PCL: 67   (PCL prepopulates %SIG with the signal names)
Emission for that line: `(defvar foo::%SIG (make-hash-table :test 'equal))`
and `(p-scalar (p-keys foo::%SIG))`.

WHY THE OBVIOUS RUNTIME FIX IS WRONG: shadowing the whole sigil-named export
set in every package PCL creates (p-defpackage) would ALSO break the
UNQUALIFIED spelling, which is load-bearing -- inside `package Foo;` an
emitted bare `|$!|` MUST be main's, and inheritance is what gives it that.
The asymmetry only exists for an EXPLICITLY qualified name, and at the CL
level both spellings are the same symbol.  So the fix is emission-side.

FIX SHAPE (not designed in detail): the emitter, when it sees a variable name
explicitly qualified into a package OTHER than main whose base name is in the
runtime's sigil-named export set, must not emit `pkg::SYMBOL`.  The natural
landing is the ONE resolver #685 just corrected -- lower it to the symref call
(`(%p-symref-hash "foo::SIG")` / `-array` / `-box`), which already answers
perl exactly; the accompanying `(defvar foo::%SIG â¦)` declaration must go with
it.  Alternative considered and NOT taken: emit a pipe-quoted symbol -- there
is no read syntax that interns a package-LOCAL symbol shadowing an inherited
one, so it cannot be expressed in the emitted form at all without a `shadow`
call, which is the same amount of runtime machinery with worse locality.

COST/BAR: this is a Pl/ EMISSION change -- generation bump, the three
checked-in artifacts regenerated, corpus-diff + the four-population
emission A/B, the full sweep and the op/ companion leg.  For ONE known row
(op/leaky-magic.t row 4, `%foo::SIG`).  Bar: leaky-magic 70/1 -> 71/0; the
unqualified spelling inside `package Foo;` must be UNCHANGED (probe `$!`,
`%SIG`, `$_`, `@INC` read and written inside a package block); `%main::SIG`
and `%::SIG` unchanged.

SCHEDULING (s451 review, W ask 2 accepted): bundle with the NEXT emission-changing round rather than spending a session -- one companion row does not price a gen bump + 3 artifacts + full sweep + op/ leg on its own.  The rejected runtime alternative above stays rejected.
CLOSED s451z, as ruled: EMISSION-side, lowered to the form the SYMBOLIC
spelling already emits -- `(p-cast-% "foo::SIG")` -- so the runtime side is
#685's resolver and nothing new.  The rejected alternatives stay rejected.

ONE predicate + one table, `Pl::ExprToCL::_foreign_runtime_global_form` /
%PCL_EXPORTED_GLOBALS (the FOURTH name table; its header points at Parser2's
%PKG_SWITCH_IMMUNE_VARS note, and the coincidence stays pinned by
Pl/t/global-partition-01.t).  Only WORD-SHAPED names: `$foo::!` is a perl
SYNTAX ERROR (probed), so the punctuation exports reach a foreign package only
symbolically.

FOUR emission sites, all existing machinery: gen_symbol_form,
_array_index_container (`$#foo::INC`), _bare_container_sym (the element path --
it already had this exact case for `$!{â¦}`), and the two slice sites.

`local` HAD to follow or the two disagree (measured: leaving it turned two
accidentally-right answers wrong).  New `deref` target kind ->
p-local-deref-hash/-array/-scalar; the subscripted and single-element paths
pass the resolver form as their container.  `p-list-=` cannot carry such a
target (it reads its LHS forms syntactically), so a solo deref takes the
aggregate assignment the symbolic spelling emits.

MEASURED: op/leaky-magic.t 70/1 -> 71/0.  46 probe rows vs perl across five
files.  corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111; emission A/B over 1036 files: exactly
op/leaky-magic.t and op/exec.t.  Guard Pl/t/symref-package-01.t rows 10-13.
subject: The LITERAL qualified spelling `%foo::SIG` still reads main's magic -- the CL READER interns it into |FOO| and finds the pcl-EXPORTED symbol INHERITED, so #685's resolver fix cannot see it (t/op/leaky-magic.t row 4, the ONE row left)
